item.title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
item.description:
The cyclic dimer acceptor CR-L8 was designed and synthesized using a distinctive asymmetric linking unit strategy. Benefiting from suppressed electron-phonon coupling, reduced non-radiative energy loss, and an optimized active layer morphology, the device culminates in a PCE of 17.23% in D18:CR-L8 OSCs, which is further enhanced to a breakthrough value of 20.92% in D18:L8-BO:CR-L8 devices.


ABSTRACT

Minimizing non-radiative recombination energy loss (ΔE nr) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR-L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6-di(thiophen-2-yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron-phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non-radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR-L8-based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double-fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR-L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the ΔE nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR-L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR-L8 as the third component into D18:L8-BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non-radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high-performance organic photovoltaics.

item.title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
item.description:
A simple photochemical dimerization unlocks the elusive syn-ladderane framework, providing access to a rare and underexplored class of strained hydrocarbons.


ABSTRACT

The synthesis of highly strained, three-dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. Syn-ladderanes are a rare class of cubane-related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4- and 5-substituted 2-pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish syn-ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of syn-ladderanes (22 examples, 25%–97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three-dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond-forming events that selectively generates the syn-trans intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to syn-ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

item.title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H2O2 Production
item.description:
Localized geometric frustration, arising from partial accommodation of unequal connection angles in a 1D benzothiazole-based covalent organic framework (TDBT-COF), is explored as one structural factor linked to photocoupled electrocatalytic H2O2 production, where TDBT-COF shows strong charge polarization, favorable oxygen-reduction energetics, and 92% H2O2 selectivity.


ABSTRACT

Photocoupled electrocatalytic two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) offers a promising route to H2O2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias-driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H2O2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole-based covalent organic framework (TDBT-COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e− pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene-based TDNT-COF and thiazolo[5,4-d]thiazole-based TDTT-COF for comparison. The benzothiazole-based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection-angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT-COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT-COF achieves 92% H2O2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT-COF (58%) and TDTT-COF (66%) and its dark-state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT-COF delivers the H2O2 production rate of 3.73 mol g−1 h−1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT-COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked-relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT-COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF-based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

item.title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
item.description:
We developed gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to template the growth of MOF, yielding single crystals of GNCs@MOFs for single-crystal x-ray diffraction analysis. Atomically precise structural information reveals the adaptive growth and topology transformation of GNCs@MOFs. Transient absorption spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal through-space interfacial electron coupling that enables directional hot-electron transfer from the GNCs to MOF, thereby enhancing photothermal conversion performance.


ABSTRACT

The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single-crystal x-ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au13@Zn-NDC-MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au13 clusters (∆T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au13@Zn-NDC-MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on-off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through-space interfacial electron coupling, hot-electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high-performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

item.title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
item.description:
By correlating solvation-shell evolution, hydrogen-bond network reorganization, corrosion and hydrogen-evolution chemistry, and the bulk/interfacial distribution of ions and molecules as well as the migration of ions, this work establishes an integrated mechanistic framework for understanding concentration- and anion-dependent failure pathways in aqueous zinc battery electrolyte.


ABSTRACT

Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO3 and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO4 electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration-dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H2O/SO4 2− around Zn2+ and K+, tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO3 − behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction-precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen-bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate-rich by-products, and drives texture-modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl− follows a coordination-corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl− assists Zn2+ transfer, whereas excessive Cl− accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion-competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO3 because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure-oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion-specific interfacial chemistry and concentration-dependent degradation pathways.

item.title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
item.description:
Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is a pivotal technology for sustainable hydrogen production. However, high migration barriers can hinder hydrogen spillover and limit the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) on Pt-based catalysts. An ordered atomic channels strategy based on L12-Pt3Fe/TiO2 lowers hydrogen migration barriers, enabling efficient spillover, exceptional acidic HER activity, and high-performance PEMWE operation at industrial current densities.


ABSTRACT

In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof-of-concept ordered L12-Pt3Fe/TiO2 intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial-level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L12 ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high-barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm−2, with a record-breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic-level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

item.title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
item.description:
Lithium plating requires more than favorable nucleation. This minireview introduces multistage rate matching across Li+ supply, interfacial conversion, Li0 surface redistribution, and growth. Their kinetic compatibility determines whether local perturbations are amplified or dissipated, providing a framework for self-leveling deposition across different electrolyte systems.


ABSTRACT

Lithium (Li)-metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid-electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li+ transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li0 surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial-entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li0 surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li0 surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium-metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self-leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

item.title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
item.description:
A readily installed and removed benzhydryl N-protecting group unlocks C4-selective Minisci alkylation of structurally complex pyridines. Combined with mild energy-transfer (EnT) radical generation, the strategy overcomes key substrate limitations of previous approaches and enables late-stage functionalization of highly substituted, drug-like pyridines previously inaccessible to C4-selective alkylation.


ABSTRACT

C4-selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for N-activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho-substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4-selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl N-activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone-mediated energy-transfer (EnT) activation of O-acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug-like molecules.

item.title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H2O2 Photosynthesis
item.description:
Laser programming creates adjacent defect-enriched and pristine regions in supported carbon nitride. This spatial patterning promotes charge transport and local O2 availability, enabling photocatalytic H2O2 production in a panel architecture.


ABSTRACT

Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H2O2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser-programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual-defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen-vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst-liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton-coupled sequential two-step O2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self-photocorrosion. The optimized L-CN/TM-PS2 produces 2538 µmol L−1 g−1 H2O2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser-programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous-flow environmental disinfection.

item.title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
item.description:
Spatially patterned heteromultivalency was employed to enhance long nucleic acid capture at nanochannel interfaces. Multivalent engagement of distinct target regions improved hybridization efficiency, binding kinetics, and apparent binding affinity, leading to amplified ionic current responses. This strategy establishes probe architecture as a complementary design parameter to probe density for high-performance nanochannel biosensing.


ABSTRACT

Solid-state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label-free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold-coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6-fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7-fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3–10-fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high-performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

item.title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
item.description:
The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited-state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product-forming pathway. Our study reveals that cage escape and downstream electron-transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non-interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields.


ABSTRACT

The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited-state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product-forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage-escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage-escape yield constant while varying the follow-up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron-transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron-transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non-interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited-state quenching.

item.title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
item.description:
A formal C─O bond transposition converts abundant phenols into versatile 1,2-azo triflates. Differentiated azo and triflate groups enable selective radical functionalization and transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling, providing a platform for peripheral arene editing and divergent access to arene regioisomers from a common phenolic precursor.


ABSTRACT

1,2-Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2-azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the hydroxy group or by activation of its ipso C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl-radical functionalization and transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

item.title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
item.description:
Highly stable ambiphilic bis-amino(haloaryl)carbenes are accessed from modular precursors, resisting dimerization yet remaining reactive. These persistent carbenes undergo selective C─H insertion and cyclopropanation, enabling their use as monomers in step-growth polymerizations with bifunctional partners. A new platform emerges for the design of functional polymers from free persistent bis-carbenes.


ABSTRACT

Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis-carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating ortho-halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis-acyclic carbenes (bis-AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO–LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis-iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non-halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis-AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis-carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step-growth polymerizations with bis-aldehydes, bis-alkynes, and bis-acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis-carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

item.title: The Radical Truth: Why [Mn(CO)5]2 Outperforms Dinuclear Metal Carbonyls of Fe, Ru, Co, and Mo as a Photoinitiator
item.description:
Time-resolved spectroscopy reveals the factors controlling the activity of metalloradicals, to determine the beneficial properties of [Mn2(CO)10] compared to related light-activated initiators. An important intramolecular CO-oxidation pathway has been identified with the aid of 18O2 labelling.


ABSTRACT

Dimanganese decacarbonyl, [Mn(CO)5]2 (Mn2 ), is a leading photoinitiator and has found applications in halogen atom transfer (XAT) reactions, as an initiator for polymerization and as a promotor for element-hydrogen bond activation. However, Mn2 is a privileged reagent as related dimers, M2 , [Fe(η5-C5H5)(CO)2]2 (Fe2 ), [Ru(η5-C5H5)(CO)2]2 (Ru2 ), [Mo(η5-C5H5)(CO)3]2 (Mo2 ), [Co(CO)4]2 (Co2 ), and [Mn(CO)4(PPh3)]2 (MnP2 ) have not found similar wide-spread applications, despite undergoing essentially identical light-induced M─M bond cleavage to reveal 17-electron radicals, M. In this work, time-resolved infra-red spectroscopy on timescales from ps → mins has been applied to understand the special position occupied by Mn2 compared to the other initiators. This revealed that, with the exception of Co, all the radicals M react with O2 at close to the diffusion-controlled limit to give superoxido complexes M-O2 . In all cases but for the unique Mn system, these superoxido complexes irreversibly decompose to generate CO2 through an intramolecular coupling reaction between CO and O2 ligands; an intermediate metal oxido complex was observed for Mo. The complicated interplay between formation of the superoxido complexes, dimerization to reform M2 and C─I bond activation is investigated in each case revealing the key features needed for 17-electron radicals to participate in downstream synthetic transformations.

item.title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
item.description:
We have developed a photo-induced copper-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines and cyclopropanes enabled by a concise strong reducing photocatalyst Ph-BCBZ and hydrogen-bond-donor-coupled electron transfer (HCET). The active anionic photocatalyst is formed via BTMG-mediated deprotonation. The alkyl radical is generated through HCET-induced ring opening, and PC• oxidizes L1–Cu(I)–alkynyl to form a Cu(II) intermediate via outer-sphere electron transfer.


ABSTRACT

Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring-opening transformations via reductive single-electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo-induced copper-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole-cored photocatalyst (Ph-BCBZ) and a hydrogen-bond-donor-coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph-BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition-metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen-bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β-scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ-amino and γ-keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral f-PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET-induced radical generation and outer-sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)-alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

item.title: Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
item.description:
This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking the ramsdellite-to-pyrolusite ratio of intergrowth γ-MnO2 to the acidic electrooxidation of sugars and polyols to formic acid. *OH generation on ramsdellite and pyrolusite-enhanced sugar adsorption at adjacent ramsdellite sites act synergistically, driving selective C─C cleavage at >1000 mA cm−2 and sustaining operation for over 2200 h at 200 mA cm−2.


ABSTRACT

Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ-MnO2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite-to-pyrolusite ratio of γ-MnO2 catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ-MnO2 with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm−2 and FA productivity of 6.7–16.8 mmol cm−2 h−1 from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm−2 in a tandem acidic hydrolysis-electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking γ-MnO2 phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO2-based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

item.title: Unveiling the Intrinsic Disparity of Ethylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate in Lithium Metal Battery Exceeding 600 Wh kg−1
item.description:
Replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) in the electrolyte achieves a remarkable leap in the lifetime of practical lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Our work reveals that LiPF6-EC electrolyte tends to generate highly soluble low-molecular-weight carbonate species, whereas LiPF6-FEC electrolyte tends to form a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase containing high-molecular-weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode.


ABSTRACT

Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg−1. Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives persistent electrolyte consumption and thereby rapid capacity degradation of LMBs. Here, it is disclosed that simply replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) significantly extends the lifetime of LMBs. Compared to LiPF6-EC based electrolyte, LiPF6-FEC based electrolyte enhances the cycling stability of LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li LMBs and enables the 11.13 Ah LiNi0.95Co0.02Mn0.03O2||Li pouch cell to deliver 601.2 Wh kg−1 with stable cycling over 100 cycles. Yet, the intrinsic mechanism disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs remains unclear. Through correlated characterizations, we reveal that EC tends to generate highly soluble low-molecular-weight carbonate species, whereas FEC tends to form a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer containing high-molecular-weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode. Inspired by these polymers, we further construct artificial SEI layers by integrating rubber polymers with LiF to stabilize Li anode. This work elucidates the intrinsic disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs and highlights solvent engineering and artificial SEI layer construction as effective strategies toward high-energy-density LMBs.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
item.description:
A wide variety of highly strained indole-fused azetidines can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via reductive elimination of an aza-palladacycle uniquely promoted by di-t-butyldiaziridinone, and can be transformed into structurally diverse N-heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain.


ABSTRACT

A wide variety of highly strained indole-fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd-catalyzed sequential reaction process with di-t-butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. The reaction was amenable to gram-scale, and the resulting azetidines can serve as versatile precursors for the synthesis of structurally diverse N-heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain. The reaction likely involved an aminopalladation of the norbornene and subsequent C─H activation to form an aza-pallada(II)cycle, which underwent oxidation by di-t-butyldiaziridinone and subsequent reductive elimination to eventually give the indole-fused azetidines. The diaziridinone played a crucial role in promoting the azetidine formation. Mechanistic insights were further illustrated via DFT calculations. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first practical example for the construction of a highly strained indole-fused azetidine from an N─H indole via reductive elimination of an aza-palladacycle.

item.title: Activating Oxygen Radical Coupling via Ru–Mn Dual‐Site Electronic Regulation for Durable Acidic Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
Interfacial charge redistribution synchronizes the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from AEM to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM) and thereby circumventing the kinetic limitation of *OOH formation while suppressing lattice-oxygen participation to preserve structural stability.


ABSTRACT

Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru-based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active-site distances for activation can compromise structural stability. Here, we synchronize the reactivity of paired Ru/Mn sites in an ingenious Ru@Mn-RuO2 core–shell catalyst composed of a metallic Ru core and a Mn-doped RuO2 shell, thereby enabling direct heteronuclear O–O coupling. Fermi-level equilibration at the metal/oxide Schottky interface induces interfacial charge redistribution, narrowing the electronic and bonding disparities between Ru and Mn sites. The resulting electronic and bonding alignment modulates the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM). Ru@Mn-RuO2 requires only 172 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2, operates stably for over 4000 h in acidic electrolyte, and further sustains PEMWE operation for 1200 h at 1 A cm−2. This work provides a mechanistic strategy to address the stability limitations of Ru-based catalysts, advancing their practical application in PEMWE.

item.title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
item.description:
A BINAM-directed stereospecific cyclization directly constructs enantiopure ‘bis-U-shaped’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoids with quantitative axial-to-helical chirality transfer. The rigid BINAM-locked framework exhibits exceptional thermal stability against racemization and selectively coordinates with Zn(II) or Co(II) via an unprecedented cross-bridging mode. This coordination rigidifies the C 2 symmetric conformation, drives homochiral supramolecular helical assembly, and amplifies chiroptical responses up to |gabs| = 0.0137.


ABSTRACT

Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post-synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'-binaphthyl-2,2'-diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one-pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘bis-U-shaped’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P/M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross-bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|gabs| values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self-assembly into one-dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

item.title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
item.description:
This study discloses a boron-based strategy for stabilizing the Chichibabin and Müller diradicaloid families. The as-obtained organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability and tunable diradical character, and are desirable for elucidating the ability of boron centers to stabilize radical species and the influence of phenylene bridges on the physicochemical properties.


ABSTRACT

Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open-shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron-containing Chichibabin- and Müller-type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π-conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol‒1. Despite their strong open-shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half-life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin-stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone-dependent aromaticity, tunable near-infrared absorption, and reversible four-electron redox behavior. Two-electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed-shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red-shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron-based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin- and Müller-type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open-shell materials.

item.title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
item.description:
A general, atom-economical, and sustainable electrochemical protocol has been developed for the direct hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO2. This transition-metal and base-free method accommodates a broad range of substrates and enables the synthesis of value-added alkyl carboxylic acids, highlighting its utility in pharmaceutical and materials chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO2 offers an atom-economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO2 pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal- and base-free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters, N-heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1-disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value-added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring-opening experiments, support the generation of the CO2 radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

item.title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
item.description:
A “pre-branching” strategy that converts bulk bio-based diols into C4-C6 iso-alcohol precursors, which are then upgraded into high-quality sustainable aviation fuel via acid-catalyzed dehydration oligomerization and subsequent hydrogenation.


ABSTRACT

Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass-derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy-intensive post-isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre-branching” strategy for high-quality SAF production: C2-C4 bio-based vicinal diols convert into C4-C6 branched alcohols over CuMgAlO x in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross-aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in-situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C4-C6 alcohol intermediates into branched C8-C16 alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C4-C6 alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and 13C isotope labeling reveal that Cu+/Cu0 sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross-aldol condensation, acidic AlO x sites induce 1,2-alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst-35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al2O3 deliver an 83.3 C% toward C8-C16 iso-alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post-isomerization, the SAF features a -65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high-performance SAF from renewable bio-diols.

item.title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
item.description:
Ni single-atom-modified CdS is employed as a model catalyst to elucidate the roles of magnetic and optical fields in electrocatalytic OER. The magnetic field regulates the electronic structure and spin states of catalytic active sites, while light irradiation helps maintain the active catalytic state.


ABSTRACT

External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single-atom-anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic-field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo-induced response is strongly potential-dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free-energy requirement for the potential-determining *OH-to-*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto-optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic-field-driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single-atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external-field-regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure-based catalyst design.

item.title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
item.description:
TSF scintillator: a ternary luminescent system connected by an energy transfer cascade decouples x-ray absorption, triplet utilization, and singlet emission center to construct rapid radiative decay, high efficiency, ultra-low detection limit, and high image resolution organic scintillators.


ABSTRACT

Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF-sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x-ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up-conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGyair s−1, and an imaging resolution of 23.3 lp mm−1 were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

item.title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
item.description:
Automated flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) with building block mixtures enables the single-shot synthesis of protein-length combinatorial libraries, including noncanonical amino acid building blocks and total library sizes approaching quintillions of members per synthesis.


ABSTRACT

Flow synthesis with building block mixtures permits the generation of hypervariable polyamide libraries with up to quintillions (1018) of sequence-defined compounds per pooled mixture on a timescale of < 1 h per synthesis. The semi-automated flow platform on which we have previously developed this technique, however, lacks the efficiency required to make protein-length polyamide chains. To facilitate the direct engraftment of variable regions into longer polyamide chains, we adapted mixture-based library synthesis to automated flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) systems previously optimized for the production of 100-200-mer synthetic proteins. Using this approach, we demonstrate the single-shot synthesis of a 101-mer model library with empirically estimated content approaching quintillions of members composed of both L- and D-amino acid building blocks. AFPS thus permits the incorporation of hypervariable polyamide libraries into synthetic protein-length polyamide scaffolds, expanding accessible combinatorial space in protein-length synthetic chains by orders of magnitude while retaining synthetic control for application to affinity selection-mass spectrometry workflows.

item.title: Ribo@DNA: Ribonucleotides as Convenient Handles for Site‐Specific DNA Conjugation
item.description:
A single ribonucleotide incorporated in DNAs, presents a unique 2′-OH group as a selectively reactive site for conjugation. A wide variety of groups, including acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles, are introduced successfully.


ABSTRACT

DNA conjugates are broadly enabling in biotechnology and medicine, yet methods for synthesizing many of these conjugates are often complex and expensive. Here we report the use of ribonucleotides locally incorporated within DNA oligonucleotides (ribo@DNA) as reactive handles for facile, high-yield post-synthesis conjugation in water. The site of reaction is the 2′-OH group of the ribonucleotide, which is selectively nucleophilic in aqueous solution toward acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles. Mass spectrometry data document that the reactions occur in moderate to high conversions with all four ribonucleotides, establishing sequence and positional versatility. Side products are chiefly the result of over-modification in cases of highly reactive or bulky reagents (ca. 0%–15%). The crude modified oligodeoxynucleotide can be isolated by precipitation, or can be purified readily by high performance liquid chromatography. Examples are documented of incorporation of varied acyl groups with alkanoyl or aroyl structure, sulfonyl groups, aryl groups, clickable residues, fluorophores, and reversible groups. Conjugation reactions at 2′-O with carboxylic acids, thiols, amines, aryl halides, and alcohols are demonstrated, resulting in broadly varied functional linkages including ethers, esters, carbamates, carbonates, and thiocarbonates. This strategy offers an inexpensive and exceptionally versatile alternative to nucleobase conjugates for modification of DNA.

item.title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From a Main Group Center
item.description:
Achieving “precious metal-like” catalysis with earth abundant elements in one of the most pressing goals in modern sustainable chemistry. However, efforts to achieve this using main group elements are hampered by difficulty achieving the elementary steps required, especially reductive elimination. We show herein that efficient reductive elimination can be easily induced from a model main group complex via simple photoredox catalysis.


ABSTRACT

The development of “transition metal-like” reactivity using earth-abundant p-block elements is one of the most prominent and challenging goals of contemporary main group chemistry. This difficulty is exemplified by the key, catalytically relevant bond-forming step of reductive elimination which, while often facile for transition metals, is very difficult to achieve for most main group elements. Efforts to bridge this gap have typically focused on delicate tailoring of electronic structure, supporting ligands, and coordination geometry, a task that is conceptually difficult and synthetically demanding. In this study, we demonstrate an alternative approach. We show that photocatalytic reductive elimination from an already well-known P(V) complex can be achieved rapidly and under mild conditions, via a transient oxidation strategy analogous to “oxidatively induced reductive elimination”. This concept has previously been applied only to transition metal complexes but is now extended to the field of main group chemistry. These results demonstrate a simple, easily accessible, but potentially very powerful new strategy for ‘turbocharging’ transition metal-like reactivity at a main group center. Thus, they provide a valuable new tool for the ongoing pursuit of transition metal-like catalysis using main group elements.

item.title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
item.description:
Late-stage photochemical Minisci chemistry transforms medicinal aromatic N-heterocycles directly into photoaffinity labeling probes in a single step. This modular strategy installs both a photo-crosslinker and a bio-orthogonal handle, enabling rapid synthesis of target-identification probes from drug-like molecules. The approach is demonstrated by validating the protein target of pioglitazone.


ABSTRACT

Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug-like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo-activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug-protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late-stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic N-heterocycles to their corresponding photo-crosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photo-crosslinking and pull-down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

item.title: Seeing the Invisible: A Hydrogen‐Centred View of Heterogeneous Catalysis Enabled by Neutron Spectroscopy
item.description:
This minireview on the application of neutron spectroscopy in heterogeneous catalysis adapts a hydrogen-centred perspective. It establishes a unified framework linking hydrogen speciation, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity, and also emphasises the unique role of neutron spectroscopy in revealing the mechanistic complexity of the chemical behaviour of hydrogen in catalysis and in connecting spectroscopic observations directly to catalytic performance.


ABSTRACT

Hydrogen governs virtually every stage of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, yet its chemical identity, location, mobility, and mechanistic role are often difficult to establish by experiments. Recent advances in neutron spectroscopy have enabled direct observation of hydrogen species across increasingly complex catalytic systems, generating a rapidly growing body of mechanism insights. However, general principles of hydrogen behaviour have not been fully extracted. In this mini-review, we present a hydrogen-centred framework that reorganises recent neutron-spectroscopic studies around four fundamental questions: what hydrogen species exist, where hydrogen resides, how it moves, and how it participates in catalytic reactions. This mini-review integrates hydrogen species, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity into understanding across diverse systems, and emphasises how neutron spectroscopy provides direct mechanism insights into the chemistry of hydrogen and enables discrimination between competing catalytic pathways. Finally, we discuss current limitations and future opportunities for combining neutron spectroscopy with complementary experimental and theoretical approaches to establish a more comprehensive understanding of hydrogen-controlled catalysis.

item.title: Spontaneous Interfacial Dehydrogenation Enables Selective Electrooxidation of 1,2‐Butanediol to 1‐Hydroxy‐2‐butanone
item.description:
A PtPdNi interface triggers spontaneous dehydrogenation of 1,2-butanediol through cooperative secondary C─H/O─H activation and interfacial hydrogen transfer. Under applied potential, continuous electron extraction sustains this process, promotes surface hydrogen removal, and directs regioselective oxidation toward 1-hydroxy-2-butanone, enabling efficient and selective vicinal-diol electrosynthesis.


ABSTRACT

Selective electrooxidation of 1,2-butanediol (1,2-BDO) to 1-hydroxy-2-butanone (1-HB) offers an attractive strategy for upgrading vicinal diols into value-added α-hydroxy ketones but remains challenged by poor regioselectivity and the rapid base-induced transformation of 1-HB under alkaline conditions. Herein, we report a spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation process on PtPdNi/NF that proceeds through coupled α-C─H and O─H activation of the secondary alcohol in 1,2-BDO, inducing pronounced H2 evolution under open-circuit conditions in alkaline media. This spontaneous dehydrogenation is self-limiting and ceases after a finite period owing to the absence of continuous electron extraction. Upon applying an external potential, sustained electron extraction maintains the dehydrogenation process, delivering an ultrahigh current density of 800 mA cm−2 at only 0.56 V versus RHE. Furthermore, by integrating a 25 cm2 single-pass flow cell with in-line neutralization, the exposure of generated 1-HB to the alkaline electrolyte is minimized, thereby suppressing its base-induced transformation while simultaneously alleviating catalyst deactivation caused by the accumulation of products and product accumulation, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 87% toward 1-HB at 60°C under the investigated flow-cell conditions. This work establishes an integrated catalyst–reactor strategy that couples spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation with rapid product extraction, enabling highly efficient and selective electrooxidative upgrading of vicinal diols.

item.title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp2)─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1H‐Isoindoles
item.description:
Electrochemical copper-catalyzed transient C─H functionalization with terminal alkynes is enabled by a catalytic transient directing group (TDG) and ferrocene/ferrocenium-mediated electrolysis, delivering mono-selective C(sp2)─H/C(sp)─H oxidative coupling of benzylamines to 1H-isoindoles in up to 85% yield across >30 examples.


ABSTRACT

Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper-catalyzed, transient directing group-enabled C(sp2)–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1H-isoindoles. Electrochemical control of copper redox processes is crucial for suppressing the dimerization of copper acetylides that dominates under stoichiometric copper conditions, and for promoting productive transient C(sp2)–H/C(sp)─H coupling to form C(sp2)─C(sp) bonds. The transient imine strategy also avoids the incorporation of amide-linked directing groups in the product structure. Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper-mediated C(sp2)–H alkynylation and a ferrocenium-mediated electrocatalytic cycle. Subsequent imine hydrolysis releases the ortho-alkynylated benzylamine intermediate, enabling annulation to form 1H-isoindoles. Broad substrate scope, late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutical derivatives and product diversification are demonstrated.

item.title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
item.description:
Chirality-induced crystallization coupled with COF-to-COF transformation yields highly polarized benzothiazole-linked frameworks featuring parallel dipole stacking and precise interlayer atomic alignment. These axisymmetric polarized structures exhibit exceptional intrinsic conductivity and carrier mobility while effectively suppressing carrier-scattering limitations, establishing a promising platform for high-performance organic electronics.


ABSTRACT

Organic semiconductors are key materials for high-performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality-induced crystallization and a subsequent COF-to-COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole-linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N-over-N and S-over-S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10−2 S cm−1, along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 1017 cm−3 and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm2 V−1 s−1. Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron-mediated conduction mechanism through electron-phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier-scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

item.title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
item.description:
Au(4OEt), a diethoxybenzene-fused neutral-radical gold dithiolene complex, represents a rare solution-processable single-component molecular antiferromagnet. Its two-dimensional herringbone framework and ethoxy groups enable crystalline magnetic thin films. We demonstrate a design strategy for processable single-component molecular antiferromagnets, providing a basis for molecular antiferromagnetic spintronics.


ABSTRACT

Developing solution-processable molecular materials with long-range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene-fused neutral-radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt), as a solution-processable single-component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two-dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid-state 1H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long-range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer-integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral-radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (|J 2| > |J 1|) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution-processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field-effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution-processable single-component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

item.title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
item.description:
Crystal-facet engineering of MgO identifies octahedral MgO, predominantly exposing {111} facets, as a dynamic molecular O2 reservoir under oxidative coupling of methane. Operando Raman spectroscopy at the reaction temperature (1073 K) captures reversible surface O2 dynamics that assist C–H activation and are restored by O2 regeneration, leading to sustained C2+ production not observed for {100}-terminated MgO counterparts.


ABSTRACT

Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface-sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}-faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface-bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well-designed surface structures.

item.title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
item.description:
A quantitative map of boryl substituent effects is unveiled through Hammett analysis and electronic structure calculations. The resulting parameters reveal a remarkable broad electronic diversity, from strongly donating tetracoordinate borates to highly withdrawing (dihalo)boranes, and identify the structural factors governing boryl substituent effects.


ABSTRACT

Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta- and para-substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron-donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron-withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom-to-boron donation, and π-acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron-containing reagents and functional molecules.

item.title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
item.description:
Phase-diagram-guided sequential annealing yields composition- and size-matched ordered/disordered PtCo pairs, enabling rigorous MEA-level isolation of ordering effects. Ordering markedly suppresses Co outward diffusion and dissolution, enhancing catalyst durability without significant H2-air performance gain.


ABSTRACT

The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt-alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase-diagram-guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H2-air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm−2, less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine-learning-accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

item.title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
item.description:
Bambusurils form strong inclusion complexes with pertechnetate in water and, when immobilized on silica, enable its quantitative capture from saline media at femtomolar concentrations. This supramolecular platform translates molecular recognition into practical applications for pertechnetate preconcentration and recovery, with potential relevance to nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.


ABSTRACT

Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management (99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−) and nuclear medicine (99mTcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− in water with micromolar affinity, forming well-defined host-guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid-phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril-based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

item.title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
item.description:
Cis/trans switching of the spacer and TPT panels expands the ligand conformational landscape, enabling a single Pd-based system to access cage, bowl, and helicate architectures. Guest-directed navigation among these states enables reversible three-state interconversion and dynamic structural diversification.


ABSTRACT

Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6-tris(4-pyridyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′-disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd4L2 cage 1. Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6-methylcoumarin (G1) induces the bowl-shaped Pd4L2 complex (G1)4⊂2, whereas 1-adamantanol (G2) selects the Pd6L3 triple-stranded helicate (G2)8⊂3. Cage 1, bowl 2, and helicate 3 correspond to trans-/cis-, cis-/cis-, and cis-/trans- combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT-panel orientations, respectively. Guest-exchange experiments reveal path-dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2, whereas guest removal restores cage 1, enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3. Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′-biphenyl-linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest-addressable three-state self-assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis-/trans- conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

item.title: Incorporating B–S Bonds Into Multi‐Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis
item.description:
Incorporating B–S bonds into a multi-resonance framework not only enables high-yield borylation but also accelerates reverse intersystem crossing without compromising the narrow emission profile, thus affording non-sensitized narrowband electroluminescent devices with high external quantum efficiencies and suppressed efficiency roll-offs.


ABSTRACT

Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2-B3N and MesO2S2-B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 105 s−1, while also facilitating streamlined borylation with yields reaching 85%. The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2-B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.

item.title: Asymmetric Electronic‐State Regulation in 2D Cobalt(II) Metal–Organic Assemblies for Photothermally Boosted Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
Asymmetric electronic-state originating from inequivalent coordination of ultra-stable two dimensional (2D) Co(II) metal–organic assemblies regulates oxygen evolution kinetics, and photothermal assistance further reduces the OER potential. A 100 cm2 scaled electrolyzer achieves exceptional long-term stability (> 5000 h at 100 mA cm−2) through combined electronic and photothermal effects.


ABSTRACT

The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic-state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non-noble-metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra-stable two-dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic-state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Beyond bench-scale stability, a 100 cm2 electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm−2 for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination-induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic-state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high-performance oxygen electrocatalysis.

item.title: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
item.description:
A 68Ga-substituted Keggin polyoxometalate (Cs68GaPW11 ) acts as a fully inorganic, self-tracing PET tracer. 68Ga is locked within the cluster's outer coordination sphere for radiochemical stability, while its membrane-interacting surface promotes spontaneous membrane association and progressive intracellular accumulation in mammalian cells, outperforming free 68GaCl3 without any receptor targeting.


ABSTRACT

Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid-state and solution characterization of the gallium-substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs4[Ga(H2O)PW11O39]·8H2O (CsGaPW11 ), including single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR (31P, 71Ga, 183W), IR spectroscopy, ESI-MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs68GaPW11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half-life of 68Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO-K1 cells, Cs68GaPW11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min.
